principles:
**Shared requirement.** CI runner selection that keeps every required check meaningful on any clone of the template while covering exactly the owner-fixed OS matrix.

| # | Principle | Source | Agreement level |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Every CI job resolves to a runner in the owner-fixed OS families `ubuntu-latest, macos-latest` | `target-os-matrix` (fixed, owner 2026-09-02) | **Policy — fixed.** Must agree across all three repos in effect |
| P2 | Untrusted pull-request code from forks of a *public* repository runs only on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners | GitHub's `self-hosted-runner-security.md`; ts D-022(1) (`S6`) | **Policy.** Must agree for every public repository in the family |
| P3 | The workflow linter's configuration declares exactly what the workflows use: nothing required is missing, nothing present is inert | Prompt value test; actionlint maintainer docs | **Standard** (a correctness property of the config file); literal contents vary per repo |
| P4 | A known linter false positive is suppressed as narrowly as possible — per file and per message — with a removal trigger | py/ts suppression headers | **Standard**; the file list varies with each repo's pipeline |
| P5 | A repository generated from the template works with zero repository configuration | Template purpose; py's own fleet comment (`S9`) | **Capability** — must agree |

What must agree: P1, P2, P5 as outcomes; P3 and P4 as properties of the config file. What may vary: the concrete `paths:` keys and whether an owner funds faster runners for a private downstream copy. (The Muse leg's "fork-operability / fixed matrix / lint-clean" framing is the same three outcomes under other names; no adjudication needed.)

**Architectural alternatives compared before any configuration detail** (mechanism is the architecture here; there are no libraries):

| Alternative | P1 | P2 | P3 lint coverage | P5 zero-config | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A1 literal / `${{ matrix.os }}`** | By construction | Yes — hosted, ephemeral | **Full**: every literal and matrix value validated (`A11`) | Yes | **Recommended** |
| A2 `vars.RUNNER_*` with hosted fallback (py) | Only by owner discipline | **No** once any variable resolves to a fleet label | **Reduced**: fallback-label typos pass (`A11`) and variable-name typos pass (`A2`, `A11b`); `config-variables` recovers only the variable-name half (`A11b`), and only as a global allow-list (`A6a`) | Yes — variables are not copied into generated repos | Ranked runner-up |
| A3 identity guard (astral) | Only by owner discipline | **No** for PRs to the guarded repo (`github.repository` is the base repo) | Reduced as A2 | Functionally, but every copy inherits upstream's slug and vendor label as dead text | Rejected |
| A4/A6 larger or vendor labels as literals | **Fails** — label outside the fixed matrix | Vendor fails; larger passes | Full | **No** — generated repos without that runner queue | Excluded (Disagreement D6 for larger SKUs) |
| A5 self-hosted / ARC | Only by operator discipline | **No** — the exact case GitHub's recommendation addresses | Needs labels block | No | Excluded |

**HIGH question 1 — does D-022(1) apply equally to rs?** Yes. ts's org judgment ("Blacksmith explicitly not reused for a public template", `S6`) turns on who pays and who configures, not on minutes saved: for the zero-config consumer all mechanisms run the identical public label, so the indirection buys nothing while costing a per-job expression on every current and future job plus the whole-repo strict-`vars` coupling (`A6a`). Rust build times justify documenting the escape hatch (a one-line comment, `A12e`), not adopting the indirection. Both legs agree; the Opus leg's five reasons and the Muse leg's cost-benefit analysis converge. The observed Rust field agrees at every scale: the Opus leg's 12-repository census and the Muse leg's 7-repository survey overlap on five repositories, cover 14 distinct repositories together, and report **zero** `vars.*` runner indirections in any of the 14, including in the slowest-building projects surveyed (uv solves speed with literal premium labels and conditionals, not indirection).

**HIGH question 2 — does `actionlint.yaml` shrink to zero F056/F057 entries?** Yes, zero, **by omitting both keys**, not by writing empty lists. `A1` (hardcoded tree, no config file at all) and `A12a` (full recommended tree plus R18-shaped `vars.*` reads) exit 0 silent; `A2` proves even an expression tree needs no declaration by default. Writing `config-variables: []` is not "zero entries": it bans every `vars.*` read and rejects R18's accepted federation variables (`A7`, `S7`).

**HIGH question 3 — agreement across py, ts, rs.** The evidence supports the same hardcoded tradeoff in all three repos, because the driver — public-template zero-config service (P5) plus the platform's public-repo rule (P2) — is ecosystem-independent. py's indirection is chronological drift (it predates the Synthesis #8 judgment D-022(1) records), not a justified Python-ecosystem difference: nothing about Python makes self-hosted execution of public pull requests safer, and py's own fallback branch concedes hardcoded public labels are correct out-of-org. ts's hardcoded shape matches the recommended rs shape. Whether py converges and ts trims its dead entry is the follow-on project's call (O1–O3); this answer supplies its rationale.

**MEDIUM — the idiomatic adopted shape, for the record.** Conditional on a member-1 reversal that this decision does not recommend:

```yaml
# Only if A2 is adopted. config-variables is GLOBAL: every vars.* name
# used by ANY workflow must be listed (A6a), not just RUNNER_*.
config-variables:
  - RUNNER_UBUNTU
  - RUNNER_MACOS
  - ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID   # R18 (S7)
  - ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID      # R18 (S7)
  - ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID   # R18 (S7), optional
# NO self-hosted-runner.labels block: labels are checked only when written
# literally in runs-on:, and A2 writes them only in settings (A5).
```

No `RUNNER_WINDOWS`: Windows is outside the fixed matrix. **The list is complete against every `vars.*` read in an accepted rs workflow fixture.** R18's two accepted fixtures are the only rs candidate workflows in this programme that read `vars.*`.
